newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: David Jones says changes help Q4 pick-up.
newsitem.headline: David Jones says changes help Q4 pick-up.

text.p: A pick-up in fourth quarter sales at upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd was due to a combination of internal measures and an improving retail climate, David Jones finance director Robert Wright said on Tuesday.
"We saw through the month of May and June some fairly cold weather, which started with Mother's Day which is a always a good period to get sales, so that was positive," Wright said.
David Jones had also continued ongoing changes to its merchandise mix and made an extra investment in staffing in some stores, he told Reuters.
David Jones earlier reported sales for the fourth quarter to July 26 of A$364.2 million, up 3.3 percent on a year earlier, or 2.1 percent on a comparable stores basis.
Fifty-two-week sales were down 0.4 percent, or 3.2 percent on a comparable stores basis, at A$1.437 billion.
Sales from the David Jones stores in the fourth quarter were up 6.4 percent, but sales at John Martin outlets in South Australia were down about 25 percent.
David Jones has announced that its Elizabeth store outside Adelaide will close, and had indicated its Kilkenny store in north-west Adelaide would also close just after Christmas, Wright said.
"We're in the process of restructuring that business," he said.
Wright said he expected sales at John Martins to begin to stabilise in the first quarter of the current financial year.
David Jones, which posted a 50 percent fall in first half net profit to A$22.34 million, is due to report its full year results on September 10.
Analysts forecasts range from around A$27 million to A$35 million. David Jones reported a net profit of A$67.53 million for the year to end-July 1996.
